youtube_description:
I just got my first spray tan. In this video, I'm going to show you why you should consider getting one, who it's right for and who it's not right for, and how to do it: what it costs, what the appointment is like, how long it lasts, and my before and after photos.

See what you'd look like with a six-pack, free:
https://absbyai.com/?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=video&utm_campaign=longform&utm_content=ro19-my-first-spray-tan

What it cost me:
Premium spray tan: about $80
Contouring (extra shadowing on the abs): about $20
A cheaper studio without the contouring: about $50

Aftercare:
1. Rapid drying tan: wait 8 hours before your first shower (other tans: a full 24 hours)
2. First shower: no soap, no washcloth, no scrubbing, just rinse. Brown water coming off is normal
3. After that: no washcloths, no exfoliating face scrubs, no glycolic acid or salicylic acid
4. Stay out of the pool, the lake and the beach if you want your tan in peak condition
It lasts about 7 days.

Get the most out of it at a photo shoot:
1. Golden hour lighting, not flat noon lighting
2. A good photographer with a good camera
3. Get a pump before you shoot: push-ups, curls, ab exercises
4. Shoot fasted
5. Spend 5 to 10 minutes on your posing first

Cameras tend to flatten your definition. Definition on camera is all about contrast, so a tan makes the same physique look more defined. If you don't know where to go, ask Claude, ChatGPT or Gemini to find you the three best spray tan studios near you. I recommend the rapid drying tan: get it early in the day, and then shower before bed. That's an eight hour wait instead of 24, and you're not sleeping in your tan and destroying your sheets. And for most guys, do it sometimes, for a photo shoot, a wedding or a big event, not every week.
